title: GOD, MAKE THIS DAY FRUITFUL AND PRODUCTIVE
text: Somebody shout hallelujah. I want you to understand something this morning. There is a difference between activity and productivity. There is a difference between motion and progress. And I have come in the name of the Lord to make a distinction tonight between those who are busy and those who are fruitful. The Bible says in John chapter 15, I am the vine, ye are the branches. He that abided in me and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit. For without me, ye can do nothing. I want you to catch something. Jesus did not say without me you can do little. He said without me you can do nothing. That word nothing in the Greek is oudes. It means not even one thing. Not even a little thing. Absolutely nothing of eternal value. You see, when God created Adam, the Bible says in Genesis chapter 2 verse 15, and the Lord God took the man and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it. Before the fall, before sin entered, God positioned man for productivity. Productivity is not a cause, it is a blessing. It is when productivity is divorced from divine purpose that it becomes burdensome. But when your day is aligned with the heartbeat of heaven, when your activities are synchronized with the agenda of the almighty, then you don't just work, you produce fruit that remains. I want somebody to hear me clearly tonight. There are people who wake up every morning and they are busy from sunrise to sunset. They run from one appointment to another. They multitask. They hustle. They grind. But at the end of the year, when they look back, there is no fruit. There is motion but no progress. There is activity but no accomplishment. And I have come to prophesy to somebody tonight that the season of empty activity is over. From this day forward, everything you touch shall prosper in the name of Jesus. The reason many believers are not fruitful is because they have not understood the principle of abiding. Jesus said, abide in me. That word abide is meno in Greek. It means to remain, to dwell, to continue, to stay. It is not a visitation, it is a habitation. God is not looking for people who will visit him on Sunday morning and then leave the rest of their week in the counsel of their own wisdom. He is looking for men and women who will make his presence their permanent address. You see, fruitfulness is not a product of human effort alone. Fruitfulness is the overflow of divine connection. When you are connected to the source, fruit becomes inevitable. Look at a branch. A branch does not struggle to produce fruit. A branch does not wake up in the morning and say, "Today I must produce apples." No. When a branch is properly connected to the tree, receiving sap, receiving nutrients, receiving life from the root, fruit becomes the natural consequence of that connection. And this is what God is saying to somebody tonight, stop struggling to be fruitful, start learning to abide, and fruitfulness will be the automatic result. Somebody shout, "I receive it." Now, let me show you something profound. In Genesis chapter 1 verse 11, God said, "Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself upon the earth." Notice that God programmed fruitfulness into creation. Everything God created has the capacity to multiply, to reproduce, to bring forth fruit after its kind. But then in Genesis chapter 3, when sin entered through the disobedience of Adam, God said in verse 17, "Cursed is the ground for thy sake. In sorrow shall thou eat of it all the days of thy life. Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth today." You see, the curse did not eliminate the ground's ability to produce. It corrupted what it would produce. Instead of fruit, there would be thorns. Instead of blessing, there would be frustration. Instead of productivity, there would be toiling without results. But glory be to God, Galatians 3:13 says, "Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us, for it is written, cursed is everyone that hangeth on a tree." When Jesus died on Calvary, he did not just die for your sins. He died to break every curse that would make your life unproductive. He died to restore the original blessing of fruitfulness that God placed upon humanity before the fall. This means tonight, as a blood-bought, born-again child of the living God, you have been legally redeemed from barrenness. You have been legally redeemed from frustration. You have been legally redeemed from empty labor. And every day of your life ought to produce results that testify to the redemptive work of Jesus Christ. Let me take you to Deuteronomy chapter 28. This is the blessing chapter. Verse 3 says, "Blessed shall thou be in the city, and blessed shall thou be in the field." That means geographical location cannot stop your blessing. VERSE 4 SAYS, "BLESSED SHALL BE the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle." That means your productivity is not dependent on economic conditions. It is dependent on covenant positioning. Verse 8 says something powerful. "The Lord shall command the blessing upon thee in thy storehouses and in all that thou settest thine hand unto." Did you hear that? God does not just bless you, he commands blessing. When God commands something, demons cannot resist it. Circumstances cannot prevent it, and delays cannot stop it. It must manifest. But there is a condition. Verse 1 says, "And it shall come to pass, if thou shall hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth." The key to commanded blessing is obedience. The key to supernatural productivity is alignment with the will and word of God. Many believers pray for fruitfulness but live in disobedience. Many believers ask God to prosper their day while they are walking in compromise, living in known sin, tolerating areas of rebellion. Let me tell you tonight, God will not empower rebellion. God will not anoint disobedience. You cannot be productive in the kingdom while living outside the parameters that produce kingdom results. Jesus said in John 15:10, "If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love, even as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in his love." Obedience is the doorway to abiding, and abiding is the secret to fruitfulness. You cannot separate these things. Now, I want you to understand the principle of sowing and reaping. Galatians 6:7 says, "Be not deceived, God is not mocked, for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap." This is a spiritual law. It is as consistent as the law of gravity. When you sow corn, you don't reap wheat. When you sow in the morning, you don't reap that afternoon. There is a season between sowing and harvest. Many believers are frustrated because they want instant results. They want microwave miracles. They sow today and expect to reap tomorrow. But God does not operate in the realm of short cuts. He operates in the realm of seasons. Ecclesiastes 3:1 says, "To everything there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven." But here is what I've come to prophesy. While you are waiting for your harvest, while you are in the season between sowing and reaping, God is working. Just because you don't see fruit yet does not mean the seed is not germinating underground. Just because your breakthrough has not manifested does not mean your prayers are not working. Keep sowing. Keep obeying. Keep trusting. Your harvest is coming in the name of Jesus. Psalm 126:5 says, "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy." Some of you have been sowing in tears. You've been faithful when nobody was watching. You've been obedient when it was inconvenient. You've been giving when you barely had anything. You've been praying when heaven seems silent. You've been worshipping when your circumstances were contrary. Let me prophesy to you tonight, your season of reaping has come. Your season of weeping is over. Get ready to reap in joy. The enemy has tried to make you believe that your efforts are in vain. The devil has whispered in your ear that your prayers are not working. That your seed is wasted. That your obedience doesn't matter. But I have come to tell you that the enemy is a liar. Every seed you have sown in the kingdom is documented in heaven. Every tear you have cried in secret is bottled by God. Every sacrifice you have made in obedience is recorded in the books of eternity and payday is coming. Now, let me show you something about the anointing for productivity. In Acts 10:38, the Bible says concerning Jesus, "How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power. Who went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed of the devil for God was with him." Notice the phrase "doing good." Jesus was productive. His ministry was fruitful. Everywhere he went, things happened. Blind eyes opened. Deaf ears heard. Lame legs walked. Dead people rose. Demons fled. DISEASES VANISHED. WHY? Because God was with him. The presence of God makes you productive. The anointing of the Holy Spirit is not just for ministry. It is for daily living. The same spirit that empowered Jesus to be fruitful in ministry is available to empower you to be fruitful in your career, in your business, in your studies, in your family, in every area of your life. Romans 8:11 says, "But if the spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his spirit that dwelleth in you." The Holy Spirit gives life. He quickens. He energizes. He empowers. When the Holy Spirit is working in you, fatigue cannot stop you. Weakness cannot limit you. Impossibilities become possibilities. But many believers are trying to be productive in their own strength. They are operating on natural energy, natural wisdom, natural ability, and then they wonder why they get tired, why they get frustrated, why they hit walls. Listen to me tonight. You cannot manufacture spiritual results with natural methods. You need the anointing. Isaiah 10:27 says, "And it shall come to pass in that day that his burden shall be taken away from off thy shoulder and his yoke from off thy neck. And the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing." The anointing breaks yokes. The anointing destroys limitations. The anointing removes burdens. When you operate under the anointing, your day becomes supernaturally productive. You accomplish in hours what would take others weeks. You solve in minutes what confuses others for years. You break through where others have been stuck for decades. Why? Because the anointing makes the difference. Let me give you practical keys to making your day fruitful. Number one, begin your day with God. Proverbs 3:6 says, "In all thy ways acknowledge him and he shall direct thy paths." Before you check your phone, before you read the news, before you start planning, acknowledge God. Give him your day. Surrender your schedule. Ask him to order your steps. Jesus demonstrated this in Mark 1:35. The Bible says, "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place and there prayed." Jesus started his day with prayer. Before the demands came, before the crowds gathered, before the ministry began, he connected with the Father. If Jesus needed to pray, how much more do we need to pray? If the Son of God needed to spend time alone with the Father, how much more do we need that fellowship? Your morning prayer is not a ritual. It is a necessity. It sets the spiritual atmosphere for your entire day. Number two, prioritize according to divine wisdom, not human pressure. Proverbs 16:3 says, "Commit thy works unto the Lord and thy thoughts shall be established." Many believers are scattered because they allow other people's emergencies to dictate their day. They are controlled by emails, phone calls, last-minute requests. They spend their day responding to external pressure instead of following internal direction. But when you commit your works to the Lord, he establishes your thoughts. He gives you clarity. He shows you what is important and what is merely urgent. He helps you say no to good things so you can say yes to God things. Jesus said in Luke 4:43, "I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, for therefore am I sent." Jesus knew his assignment. He did not allow the needs of one city to keep him from his mandate. He was focused. He was intentional. He was purpose-driven. You need to know what God has called you to do. You need to know your assignment. Because when you know your assignment, you can discern which opportunities are divine and which are distractions. Number three, work with excellence. Colossians 3:23 says, "And whatsoever you do, do it heartily as to the Lord and not unto men." Excellence is not perfection. It is giving your best. It is doing what you do with your whole heart, knowing that God is watching. Daniel 6:3 says concerning Daniel, "Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes because an excellent spirit was in him." An excellent spirit. Daniel did not do sloppy work. He did not cut corners. He did not make excuses. He gave his best and his excellence made him stand out. If you are a student, study with excellence. If you are an employee, work with excellence. If you are a business owner, serve with excellence. Let the quality of your work be a testimony to the God you serve. Let people see your diligence and glorify your Father in heaven. Number four, be sensitive to the Holy Spirit throughout your day. Romans 8:14 says, "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons OF GOD." THE HOLY SPIRIT WANTS TO GUIDE YOU. HE WANTS TO LEAD YOU to the right conversations, the right decisions, the right opportunities. Sometimes the Holy Spirit will prompt you to call someone and that call opens a door. Sometimes it will prompt you to go somewhere and you meet someone who becomes a divine connection. Sometimes it will prompt you to sow a seed and that seed unlocks a breakthrough. But you must be sensitive. You must be listening. Acts 16:6-7 tells us that Paul and his team were forbidden by the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia. Then they tried to go to Bithynia, but the spirit suffered them not. The Holy Spirit was redirecting them and because they obeyed, they ended up in Macedonia where a great revival broke out. What if they had ignored the Holy Spirit? What if they had insisted on their own plans? They would have missed the divine assignment. Your productivity is connected to your sensitivity. Learn to hear his voice. Learn to obey his promptings. Learn to flow with his leading. Number five, redeem your time. Ephesians 5:16 says, "Redeeming the time because the days are evil. Time is your most valuable resource. You can make more money, but you cannot make more time. Once a day is gone, it is gone forever. You cannot rewind it. You cannot replay it. You cannot recover it. This is why you must be intentional about how you use your time. Stop wasting hours on social media, scrolling through things that don't edify you. Stop spending your evenings watching programs that fill your mind with garbage. Stop giving your time to relationships that drain you and don't add value. Psalm 90:12 says, "So teach us to number our days that we may apply our hearts onto wisdom." Number your days. Be aware of how you spend your time. Be deliberate. Be purposeful. Every day counts. Every hour matters. Every minute is an opportunity to advance the kingdom or waste your life. Now, let me address some enemies of productivity. The first enemy is distraction. Distraction is anything that pulls your focus away from what God has called you to do. It can be good things, but they are not God things for you at this time. Martha was distracted in Luke 10. She was doing good things, cooking, serving, preparing, but Jesus said, "Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful, and Mary had chosen that good part." Mary chose to sit at Jesus' feet. She chose communion over activity, and Jesus honored her choice. Sometimes you need to stop doing and start being. Sometimes you need to stop working and start worshiping. Sometimes you need to stop running and start resting in His presence, because it is in His presence that you receive direction for your activities. The second enemy is procrastination. Proverbs 6:9-11 says, "How long will thou sleep, oh sluggard? When will thou arise out of thy sleep? Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep, so shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man." Procrastination is a thief. It steals your opportunities. It robs your potential. It kills your dreams. Every time you say, "I'll do it tomorrow," you are gambling with your destiny, because tomorrow is not promised. Proverbs 27:1 says, "Boast not thyself of tomorrow, for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth." If God has given you an assignment, do it now. If the Holy Spirit has prompted you to take an action, obey now. Don't wait for perfect conditions. Don't wait until you feel ready. Don't wait until everything makes sense. Obey now. The third enemy is fear. Fear paralyzes. Fear immobilizes. Fear makes you second-guess yourself. Fear makes you doubt your calling. Fear makes you shrink back from opportunities. But 2 Timothy 1:7 says, "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind." Fear is not from God. Fear is from the enemy, and you must refuse to bow to it. Joshua 1:9 says, "Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage. Be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed, for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest." God is with you. If God is with you, what can man do to you? If God is for you, who can be against you? Step out. Take that risk. Launch that business. Write that book. Start that ministry. Apply for that position. Make that call. Stop allowing fear to keep you trapped in unproductive living. The fourth enemy is unforgiveness. Unforgiveness is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. It doesn't hurt them. It hurts you. It clogs your spiritual arteries. It blocks the flow of God's blessing in your life. Mark 11:25 says, "And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any, that your Father also, which is in heaven, may forgive you your trespasses." Unforgiveness affects your prayer life. It affects your worship. It affects your productivity. If you want God to make your day fruitful, you must release every person who has hurt you. Forgive that colleague who betrayed you. Forgive that family member who disappointed you. Forgive that friend who abandoned you. Let it go. Release them into God's hands. Free yourself. Now, let me pray prophetically over your life. But before I pray, I want you to lift up your hands. I want you to open your mouth. I want you to agree with every word I speak, because the prayer of agreement releases power. Matthew 18:19 says, "If two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven." Father, in the name of Jesus, I come before your throne of grace with boldness. I thank you for every person reading this word right now. I thank you that they are not here by accident. They are here by divine appointment, and I speak over their lives tonight. I decree and declare that from this day forward, every day of their life shall be fruitful. Every day shall be productive. Every day shall count for eternity. I release the anointing of the Holy Spirit upon their activities. I release divine wisdom. I release supernatural strategies. I release uncommon ideas. Lord, I pray that you will remove every distraction, every time waster, every energy drainer. Separate them from relationships that are not ordained by you. Deliver them from procrastination. Break the spirit of fear. Uproot every seed of doubt. I speak to barren wombs in the realm of the spirit, conceive. I speak to dry grounds, bring forth. I speak to unproductive lives, be fruitful. In the name of Jesus, Father, I pray for divine connections. Bring them into contact with people who will open doors, people who will invest in their vision, people who will mentor them, people who will partner with them. Let divine appointments fill their calendar. I decree that they shall be in the right place at the right time. They shall say the right words to the right people. They shall make decisions that align with your will. Their steps shall be ordered by you. I break every curse of frustration. I break every curse of empty labor. I break every generational pattern of unproductivity. I command it to lose its hold in Jesus' name. I speak supernatural acceleration. What would have taken them 10 years, they shall accomplish in 1 year. What would have taken them months, they shall accomplish in weeks. They shall mount up with wings as eagles. They shall run and not be weary. They shall walk and not faint. I decree that favor shall locate them. Favor with God and favor with man. Doors that have been shut shall open. Opportunities that have been hidden shall be revealed. Resources that have been blocked shall be released. Lord, anoint their hands. Whatever they touch shall prosper. Anoint their mind. Every thought shall be productive. Anoint their mouth. Every word shall carry weight. Anoint their steps. Every path shall lead to success. I release the spirit of diligence, the spirit of excellence, the spirit of creativity, the spirit of innovation. Let ideas flow. Let solutions come. Let breakthroughs manifest. Every satanic agenda to waste their time fail. Every demonic plot to frustrate their efforts backfire. Every evil plan to make them unproductive be destroyed in the mighty name of Jesus. I decree that at the end of this year, they shall have testimony. They shall have results. They shall have fruit, fruit that remains, fruit that multiplies, fruit that glorifies your name. Father, I thank you because your word says in Isaiah 55:11, "So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth. It shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it." Every word I have spoken tonight shall accomplish its purpose. It shall not return void. It shall produce results in Jesus mighty name. Now, I want you to receive this word by faith. I want you to seal it with a shout of praise. Open your mouth right now and give God the highest praise. Thank him for what he has done. Thank him for what he's doing. Thank him for what he's about to do. Some of you need to make some adjustments. You need to wake up earlier to pray. You need to cut off some relationships. You need to change your schedule. You need to repent of time-wasting habits. Do it now. Don't wait. Your fruitfulness depends on your obedience. Remember, fruitfulness is not optional for the believer. It is mandatory. Jesus said in John 15:16, "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you and ordained you that ye should go and bring forth fruit and that your fruit should remain." You are ordained to be fruitful. It is your destiny. It is your design. It is your divine assignment. From this day forward, measure your days by fruit, not by activity. Measure your success by kingdom impact, not by human applause. Measure your productivity by eternal value, not by earthly accumulation. And I prophesy, your best days are ahead of you. Your most productive season is coming. Your greatest fruit is yet to be harvested. Get ready. Position yourself. Align yourself. Your time has come. Somebody shout, "Hallelujah!" Give God the glory. Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. Your day is fruitful. Your day is productive. Your day counts in Jesus mighty name. Amen and amen.
